rektion: jdn. wiederbeleben; fig.: etw. (Akk.) wiederbeleben (eine Tradition, die Innenstadt)
meaning_en: to resuscitate, to revive; fig.: to revive (a tradition)
definition_de: einen bewusstlosen Menschen, dessen Herz nicht mehr schlägt, wieder zum Leben bringen (mit Herzdruckmassage); übertragen: etwas Altes wieder lebendig machen (eine Tradition wiederbeleben). Nur trennbar (Perfekt: wiederbelebt); eine untrennbare Form gibt es nicht.
example_de: Eine Passantin hat den bewusstlosen Jogger im Park wiederbelebt, kurz bevor der Krankenwagen kam.
example_en: A passer-by resuscitated the unconscious jogger in the park just before the ambulance arrived.
visual_idea: Collocation 'jdn. wiederbeleben' (Erste Hilfe): the result state shows the jogger opening his eyes while the helper sits back relieved, with the ambulance arriving behind, so back-to-life is visible and all sentence nouns are in frame. Rejected: 'eine Tradition wiederbeleben' (a folk festival reads as 'feiern') and 'die Innenstadt wiederbeleben' (abstract). Unconscious to awake is a change, so a first+last-frame video starts with the CPR.
image_prompt: low side view of a park path with green lawn, a red and white ambulance stopping on the road in the background with its blue lights on; a young woman with a brown ponytail in a blue jacket kneels beside a man in a grey running shirt lying on his back on the path; the man has just opened his eyes and lifts his head slightly, coughing; the woman sits back on her heels with a deeply relieved smile, one hand on his shoulder
negative_prompt: text, letters, watermark, signature, caption, blurry, extra fingers, deformed hands, cluttered background, multiple panels
video_start_prompt: low side view of a park path with green lawn, a red and white ambulance stopping on the road in the background with its blue lights on; a young woman with a brown ponytail in a blue jacket kneels beside a man in a grey running shirt lying on his back on the path; the man's eyes are closed and his face is pale; the woman leans over him with straight arms and presses both hands on the centre of his chest
